records.source: וְאֵ֣לֶּה׀מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכּ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּֽרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־אַרְצָ֔ם בְּעֵ֥בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן מִזְרְחָ֣ה הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ מִנַּ֤חַל אַרְנוֹן֙ עַד־הַ֣ר חֶרְמ֔וֹן וְכָל־הָעֲרָבָ֖ה מִזְרָֽחָה׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] kings of the land whom struck down [the] sons of Israel, and they took possession of their land across the Jordan toward [the] rising of the sun, from [the] wadi of Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:
pieces: These are the kings of the land whom the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated and whose land they took possession of across the Jordan, toward the sunrise, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, with all the Arabah on the east:

L.1: Now these [are] the kings of the land whom the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck down, and whose land they took possession of across the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the wadi of Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward:

R.1: Here are the kings of the land whom the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated. The Israelites took over their land on the east side of the Jordan River. It reached from the Arnon River in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, and it took in the whole eastern side of the Jordan Valley.

decisions.choice: struck down: defeated in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or hit, and with kings and armies it means to defeat them in war. The list that follows counts the kings Israel overcame, first those east of the Jordan under Moses (verses 1-6), then those west of it under Joshua (verses 7-24).

decisions.choice: across the Jordan toward the sunrise: the land east of the river
decisions.reason: "Across the Jordan" means the other side of the river. Here the words "toward the rising of the sun" show that the east side is meant; in verse 7 the same phrase is joined to "westward" and means the west side. The direction word, not the phrase itself, settles which bank is in view.

decisions.choice: from the Arnon to Hermon, with the eastern Arabah: the full reach of the land east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The Arnon is the deep gorge that runs into the Dead Sea from the east and was Moab's northern border (Numbers 21:13). Mount Hermon is the high mountain far to the north. The Arabah is the deep rift valley of the Jordan; "eastward" limits it to the part on the east side of the river (Deuteronomy 3:8, 17).

decisions.choice: the Arnon River in the south ... Mount Hermon in the north ... the Jordan Valley
decisions.reason: Readable adds "in the south" and "in the north" so a reader can picture the span, and calls the Arabah "the Jordan Valley", the part of it in view here, as Deuteronomy 3:17 does.

records.heading: The kings defeated east of the Jordan

records.source: סִיחוֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י הַיּוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן מֹשֵׁ֡ל מֵעֲרוֹעֵ֡ר אֲשֶׁר֩ עַל־שְׂפַת־נַ֨חַל אַרְנ֜וֹן וְת֤וֹךְ הַנַּ֨חַל֙ וַחֲצִ֣י הַגִּלְעָ֔ד וְעַד֙ יַבֹּ֣ק הַנַּ֔חַל גְּב֖וּל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Sihon king of the Amorite[s], the [one] dwelling in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer, which [is] on [the] edge of [the] wadi of Arnon, and [the] middle of the wadi, and half of the Gilead, and to Jabbok the wadi, [the] border of [the] sons of Ammon,
pieces: Sihon king of the Amorites, whose city was Heshbon. His rule reached from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the middle of the valley, over half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.

L.2: Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, ruling from Aroer, which [is] on the edge of the wadi of Arnon, and [from] the middle of the wadi, and half of Gilead, and as far as the wadi Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon;

R.2: One was Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in the city of Heshbon. He ruled the land from the town of Aroer, at the edge of the Arnon River valley, and from the middle of that valley. His land took in half of Gilead, as far north as the Jabbok River, where the land of the Ammonites began.

decisions.choice: Sihon king of the Amorites, ruling from Heshbon
decisions.reason: Sihon refused to let Israel pass through his land, fought them and was defeated (Numbers 21:21-31; Deuteronomy 2:24-37). Heshbon was his royal city, which he had taken from Moab (Numbers 21:26).

decisions.choice: the middle of the wadi: probably the town that stood in the valley
alternatives: the middle of the stream bed as the boundary
decisions.reason: The words are brief. Joshua 13:9 and 13:16 speak of "the city that is in the middle of the valley" next to Aroer, so this is probably that town; the phrase could also mean the middle of the stream bed, marking the border line. The translation keeps the short wording.

decisions.choice: half of Gilead, as far as the Jabbok, the Ammonite border
decisions.reason: Gilead is the hill country east of the Jordan. The Jabbok cuts across it; Sihon held the half south of it and Og the half to the north (verse 5). The upper course of the Jabbok bends south and marked the western edge of Ammon's land (Deuteronomy 3:16).

decisions.choice: His rule reached ... / One was Sihon ... His land took in
decisions.reason: The Hebrew runs the description on with participles ("dwelling ... ruling"). Balanced starts a new sentence ("His rule reached"); Readable also adds "One was" to tie Sihon to the kings named in verse 1, and "as far north as" to show the direction.

records.source: וְהָעֲרָבָה֩ עַד־יָ֨ם כִּנְר֜וֹת מִזְרָ֗חָה וְ֠עַד יָ֣ם הָעֲרָבָ֤ה יָם־הַמֶּ֨לַח֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה דֶּ֖רֶךְ בֵּ֣ית הַיְשִׁמ֑וֹת וּמִ֨תֵּימָ֔ן תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדּ֥וֹת הַפִּסְגָּֽה׃
records.gloss: and the Arabah to [the] sea of Chinneroth eastward, and to [the] sea of the Arabah, [the] sea of the salt, eastward, [the] way of Beth-jeshimoth, and from [the] south under [the] slopes of the Pisgah.
pieces: He also ruled the Arabah on the east, from the Sea of Chinneroth down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Dead Sea, in the direction of Beth-jeshimoth, and southward below the slopes of Pisgah.

L.3: and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth eastward, and as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, eastward, [in the] direction of Beth-jeshimoth, and from the south below the slopes of Pisgah.

R.3: He also ruled the eastern side of the Jordan Valley, from Lake Chinneroth, which is the Sea of Galilee, down to the Dead Sea, toward the town of Beth-jeshimoth. In the south his land reached to the foot of Mount Pisgah.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Chinneroth, the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea
decisions.reason: The Sea of Chinneroth is the lake later called the Sea of Galilee (Numbers 34:11). The Sea of the Arabah and the Salt Sea are two names for the Dead Sea, at the south end of the Jordan valley. The verse traces the eastern side of the valley from the one lake to the other, as Deuteronomy 3:17 does.

decisions.choice: from the south: the direction, not a place name
decisions.reason: The word can be the name of a region of Edom (Teman), but here it names the direction: the southern end of Sihon's land lay below the slopes of Pisgah, the ridge overlooking the Dead Sea from the east (Deuteronomy 3:17; 34:1).

decisions.choice: He also ruled
decisions.reason: The Hebrew simply adds "and the Arabah" to the list of what Sihon ruled in verse 2. Balanced and Readable repeat the verb so the new sentence reads clearly. Readable also gives the familiar names of the two lakes.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the modern name for the Salt Sea, as in 3:16 and 15:2. Literal keeps "Salt Sea".

records.source: וּגְב֗וּל ע֚וֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֔ן מִיֶּ֖תֶר הָרְפָאִ֑ים הַיּוֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּעַשְׁתָּר֖וֹת וּבְאֶדְרֶֽעִי׃
records.gloss: And [the] territory of Og king of the Bashan, of [the] remnant of the Rephaim, the [one] dwelling in Ashtaroth and in Edrei,
pieces: They also took the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and Edrei.

L.4: And the territory of Og king of Bashan, [one] of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,

R.4: They also took the land of Og, the king of Bashan. He was one of the last of the Rephaim, a people known for their great size. He lived in the towns of Ashtaroth and Edrei.

decisions.choice: and the territory of Og: a second item after Sihon in the list begun in verse 1
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb of its own. It continues the list of what Israel took east of the Jordan, so "took possession of" from verse 1 is understood.

decisions.choice: of the remnant of the Rephaim: one of the last of an ancient people remembered for their height
decisions.reason: The Rephaim were an early people of the lands east of the Jordan, known for their great size (Deuteronomy 2:10-11, 20-21). Og was the last of them (Deuteronomy 3:11).

decisions.choice: Og, who lived at Ashtaroth and Edrei
decisions.reason: Og was defeated at Edrei after Sihon (Numbers 21:33-35; Deuteronomy 3:1-11). Ashtaroth and Edrei were his royal towns in Bashan, the fertile plateau north of Gilead (13:12; Deuteronomy 1:4).

decisions.choice: They also took
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb understood from verse 1. Readable adds a short note on who the Rephaim were, as Deuteronomy 3:11 does.

records.source: וּ֠מֹשֵׁל בְּהַ֨ר חֶרְמ֤וֹן וּבְסַלְכָה֙ וּבְכָל־הַבָּשָׁ֔ן עַד־גְּב֥וּל הַגְּשׁוּרִ֖י וְהַמַּעֲכָתִ֑י וַחֲצִי֙ הַגִּלְעָ֔ד גְּב֖וּל סִיח֥וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: and ruling over Mount Hermon and over Salecah and over all the Bashan to [the] border of the Geshurite[s] and the Maacathite[s], and half of the Gilead, [the] border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
pieces: He ruled over Mount Hermon, Salecah and all of Bashan, up to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and over half of Gilead, up to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

L.5: and ruling over Mount Hermon and over Salecah and over all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, [to the] border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

R.5: He ruled over Mount Hermon, the town of Salecah and all of Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He also ruled the other half of Gilead, up to the border of King Sihon of Heshbon.

decisions.choice: the Geshurites and the Maacathites: small peoples on the north-eastern edge of Bashan
decisions.reason: These two peoples lived beyond Bashan to the north and east. Israel did not drive them out, and they went on living among Israel (13:11, 13; Deuteronomy 3:14).

decisions.choice: half of Gilead, to the border of Sihon: the northern half
decisions.reason: Og held the half of Gilead north of the Jabbok, which met the half held by Sihon (verse 2; Deuteronomy 3:12-13).

decisions.choice: the other half of Gilead
decisions.reason: Readable says "the other half" to make clear that this is not the half of Gilead that Sihon ruled in verse 2.

records.source: מֹשֶׁ֧ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֛ה וּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הִכּ֑וּם וַֽ֠יִּתְּנָהּ מֹשֶׁ֨ה עֶֽבֶד־יְהוָ֜ה יְרֻשָּׁ֗ה לָרֻֽאוּבֵנִי֙ וְלַגָּדִ֔י וְלַחֲצִ֖י שֵׁ֥בֶט הַֽמְנַשֶּֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: Moses, [the] slave of Yahweh, and [the] sons of Israel struck them down, and gave it Moses, [the] slave of Yahweh, [as a] possession to the Reubenite[s] and to the Gadite[s] and to [the] half [of the] tribe of the Manasseh.
pieces: Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated them, and Moses the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

L.6: Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck them down, and Moses the slave of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave it as a possession to the Reubenites and to the Gadites and to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

R.6: Moses, the servant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had defeated these two kings. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and to half of the tribe of Manasseh to be their own.

decisions.choice: the slave of the LORD: one who belongs wholly to the LORD, a title of honor
decisions.reason: The word is used of a servant who belongs to his master, not one who is hired. Said of Moses (1:1, 13, 15; Deuteronomy 34:5) it marks him as the LORD's own servant, acting with his master's authority.

decisions.choice: gave it as a possession to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Moses gave the land east of the Jordan to these tribes on condition that their fighting men crossed with the rest of Israel (Numbers 32; Joshua 1:12-15). The gift is described in detail in 13:8-32.

decisions.choice: it: the land of the two kings
decisions.reason: The pronoun is feminine singular and refers to the land, the word used in verse 1.

decisions.choice: slave (Literal), servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: This follows the project's rule for this word. Readable gives the title once and supplies "these two kings" and "their land" so the pronouns are clear.

records.source: וְאֵ֣לֶּה מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֡רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֩ הִכָּ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ יָ֔מָּה מִבַּ֤עַל גָּד֙ בְּבִקְעַ֣ת הַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וְעַד־הָהָ֥ר הֶחָלָ֖ק הָעֹלֶ֣ה שֵׂעִ֑ירָה וַיִּתְּנָ֨הּ יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ לְשִׁבְטֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרֻשָּׁ֖ה כְּמַחְלְקֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And these [are the] kings of the land whom struck down Joshua and [the] sons of Israel across the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in [the] valley of the Lebanon and to the mountain the Halak, the [one] going up to Seir; and gave it Joshua to [the] tribes of Israel [as a] possession according to their divisions,
pieces: These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated across the Jordan on the west side, from Baal-gad in the Lebanon Valley up to Mount Halak, the mountain that rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession, portion by portion,

L.7: And these [are] the kings of the land whom Joshua and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck down across the Jordan westward, from Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which goes up toward Seir; and Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,

R.7: Here are the kings whom Joshua and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated on the west side of the Jordan River. Their land reached from Baal-gad in the Lebanon Valley in the north to Mount Halak, which rises toward the land of Seir in the south. Joshua gave this land to the tribes of Israel to be their own, and he divided it among them.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan westward: the land west of the river
decisions.reason: The same phrase that meant the east side in verse 1 here has "westward" with it, so the land of Canaan proper is meant, where Israel now was.

decisions.choice: from Baal-gad to Mount Halak: the northern and southern limits of Joshua's conquests
decisions.reason: The same limits are given in 11:17. Baal-gad lay in the valley below Mount Hermon, in the far north. Mount Halak, "the bare mountain", rose toward Seir, the hill country of Edom, in the far south.

decisions.choice: divisions: the portions allotted to each tribe
decisions.reason: The word means a share or division. It points ahead to the dividing of the land among the tribes in chapters 13-21 (11:23; 18:10).

decisions.choice: in the north ... in the south
decisions.reason: Readable adds the directions so a reader can picture the span of the land.

records.heading: The kings defeated west of the Jordan

records.source: בָּהָ֣ר וּבַשְּׁפֵלָ֗ה וּבָֽעֲרָבָה֙ וּבָ֣אֲשֵׁד֔וֹת וּבַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וּבַנֶּ֑גֶב הַֽחִתִּי֙ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַפְּרִזִּ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃פ
records.gloss: in the hill country and in the Shephelah and in the Arabah and in the slopes and in the wilderness and in the Negev, the Hittite[s], the Amorite[s] and the Canaanite[s], the Perizzite[s], the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s].
pieces: in the hill country and the foothills, in the Arabah and on the slopes, in the wilderness and in the Negev, the land of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.

L.8: in the hill country and in the Shephelah and in the Arabah and on the slopes and in the wilderness and in the Negev, the Hittites, the Amorites and the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.

R.8: This land was in the hill country, the low hills in the west, the Jordan Valley, the hillsides, the desert, and the dry country in the south. It was the land where the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites lived.

decisions.choice: hill country, Shephelah, Arabah, slopes, wilderness, Negev: the regions of the land west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The central hill country; the Shephelah, the low hills between the hills and the coastal plain; the Arabah, the Jordan valley; the slopes that fall from the hills to the valleys; the wilderness of Judah; and the Negev, the dry south (10:40; 11:16; Deuteronomy 1:7).

decisions.choice: Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites: the peoples of the land
decisions.reason: This is the usual list of the nations of Canaan (9:1; 11:3; Exodus 3:8). Here it names the land by the peoples who lived in it, without a verb.

decisions.choice: the land of the Hittites ... / It was the land where ... lived
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "the land of" so the peoples' names read as a description of the land. Readable also describes the Shephelah, the Arabah and the Negev instead of naming them, as Deuteronomy 1:7 does.

records.source: מֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיח֖וֹ אֶחָ֑ד מֶ֧לֶךְ הָעַ֛י אֲשֶׁר־מִצַּ֥ד בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Jericho, one; king of the Ai, which [is] from [the] side of Bethel, one;
pieces: The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is near Bethel, one;

L.9: the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which [is] beside Bethel, one;

R.9: The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is near Bethel, one;

decisions.choice: one: a tally, counting each king in turn
decisions.reason: Each line of the list ends with "one", like an entry in a count, and the total is given at the end (verse 24). The repeated word is kept at every level so the list keeps its form.

decisions.choice: Jericho and Ai, near Bethel: the first two cities taken
decisions.reason: Jericho fell in chapter 6 and Ai in chapter 8; Ai lay close to Bethel, east of it (7:2; 8:9).

decisions.choice: the king of X, one;
decisions.reason: The list keeps the Hebrew formula at every level, with a semicolon after each entry, so the count can be followed to its total in verse 24. Balanced and Readable say "which is near Bethel" for Literal's "beside".

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ חֶבְר֖וֹן אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Jerusalem, one; king of Hebron, one;
pieces: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;

L.10: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;

R.10: the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;

decisions.choice: Jerusalem and Hebron: two of the five kings of the southern alliance
decisions.reason: Their kings joined the attack on Gibeon and were put to death at Makkedah (10:3-5, 22-27). As in verse 9, "one" counts each king.

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ יַרְמוּת֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ לָכִ֖ישׁ אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Jarmuth, one; king of Lachish, one;
pieces: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;

L.11: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;

R.11: the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;

decisions.choice: Jarmuth and Lachish: two more of the five kings
decisions.reason: Both kings were among the five of 10:3-5, 23. Lachish itself was taken in 10:31-32.

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ עֶגְלוֹן֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ גֶּ֖זֶר אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Eglon, one; king of Gezer, one;
pieces: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;

L.12: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;

R.12: the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;

decisions.choice: Eglon and Gezer
decisions.reason: The king of Eglon was the last of the five (10:3, 34-35). Horam king of Gezer came to help Lachish and was struck down (10:33), though Gezer itself was not taken (16:10).

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ דְּבִר֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ גֶּ֖דֶר אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Debir, one; king of Geder, one;
pieces: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;

L.13: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;

R.13: the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;

decisions.choice: Debir and Geder
decisions.reason: Debir was taken in 10:38-39. Geder appears only here, and where it lay is not known.

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ חָרְמָה֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ עֲרָ֖ד אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Hormah, one; king of Arad, one;
pieces: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;

L.14: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;

R.14: the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;

decisions.choice: Hormah and Arad: towns in the Negev
decisions.reason: The king of Arad attacked Israel in the wilderness, and the place of his defeat was named Hormah (Numbers 21:1-3; compare Judges 1:16-17).

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ לִבְנָה֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ עֲדֻלָּ֖ם אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Libnah, one; king of Adullam, one;
pieces: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;

L.15: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;

R.15: the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;

decisions.choice: Libnah and Adullam: towns of the Shephelah
decisions.reason: Libnah was taken in 10:29-30. Adullam is not named in the battle accounts; it lay in the low hills of Judah (15:35; Genesis 38:1).

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ מַקֵּדָה֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Makkedah, one; king of Bethel, one;
pieces: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;

L.16: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;

R.16: the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;

decisions.choice: Makkedah and Bethel
decisions.reason: Makkedah was taken in 10:28. The men of Bethel joined Ai against Israel (8:17); the capture of the town is told in Judges 1:22-26.

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ תַּפּ֨וּחַ֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ חֵ֖פֶר אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Tappuah, one; king of Hepher, one;
pieces: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;

L.17: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;

R.17: the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;

decisions.choice: Tappuah and Hepher: towns of the central hills and plain
decisions.reason: Neither town is named in the battle accounts. Tappuah lay on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh (16:8; 17:7-8); Hepher was a district later named in 1 Kings 4:10.

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ אֲפֵק֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ לַשָּׁר֖וֹן אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Aphek, one; king of the Sharon, one;
pieces: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;

L.18: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;

R.18: the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;

decisions.choice: Lasharon: read as a town name, though it may mean "of the Sharon"
alternatives: the king of Aphek in the Sharon
decisions.reason: The word is the name Sharon with a small word meaning "of" or "belonging to" joined to it. It may be the name of a town, Lasharon, or it may mean "the king of the Sharon", the coastal plain where Aphek stood, so that the two entries describe one king of Aphek in the Sharon. The ancient Greek translation reads it in this second way. The translation keeps the name as a separate entry, since the count of thirty-one in verse 24 needs it.

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ מָדוֹן֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ חָצ֖וֹר אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Madon, one; king of Hazor, one;
pieces: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;

L.19: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;

R.19: the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;

decisions.choice: Madon and Hazor: the leaders of the northern alliance
decisions.reason: Jabin king of Hazor called the northern kings together, Jobab king of Madon among them (11:1-5). Hazor was taken and burned (11:10-11).

records.source: מֶ֣לֶךְ שִׁמְר֤וֹן מְראוֹן֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ אַכְשָׁ֖ף אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Shimron-meron, one; king of Achshaph, one;
pieces: the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;

L.20: the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;

R.20: the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;

decisions.choice: Shimron-meron and Achshaph: towns of the northern alliance
decisions.reason: Kings of Shimron and Achshaph were among those Jabin summoned (11:1). Shimron-meron is probably the same Shimron under a fuller name.

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ תַּעְנַךְ֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶ֥לֶךְ מְגִדּ֖וֹ אֶחָֽד׃

pieces: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;

L.21: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;

R.21: the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;

decisions.choice: Taanach and Megiddo: towns guarding the passes into the Jezreel valley
decisions.reason: Neither is named in the battle accounts, and their people were not driven out for a long time (17:11-12; Judges 1:27).

records.source: מֶ֤לֶךְ קֶ֨דֶשׁ֙ אֶחָ֔ד מֶֽלֶךְ־יָקְנֳעָ֥ם לַכַּרְמֶ֖ל אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Kedesh, one; king of Jokneam of the Carmel, one;
pieces: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;

L.22: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;

R.22: the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;

decisions.choice: Kedesh, and Jokneam in Carmel
decisions.reason: Kedesh was a town in the hills of Galilee (19:37; 20:7). Jokneam lay at the foot of Mount Carmel, near the coast; "in Carmel" places it by the mountain (19:11).

records.source: מֶ֥לֶךְ דּ֛וֹר לְנָפַ֥ת דּ֖וֹר אֶחָ֑ד מֶֽלֶךְ־גּוֹיִ֥ם לְגִלְגָּ֖ל אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: King of Dor of [the] height of Dor, one; king of Goiim of Gilgal, one;
pieces: the king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;

L.23: the king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;

R.23: the king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;

decisions.choice: Dor in Naphath-dor: the coastal town of Dor and its district
decisions.reason: Dor was a harbor town south of Mount Carmel. Naphath-dor, perhaps "the heights of Dor", is the district around it, named among the northern allies in 11:2.

decisions.choice: Goiim in Gilgal, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: the king of Goiim in Galilee
decisions.reason: Goiim means "nations" and is used as a name, as in "Tidal king of Goiim" (Genesis 14:1). This Gilgal is probably not Israel's camp near Jericho (4:19), since the king is listed among the northern ones. The ancient Greek translation has "Galilee" in place of Gilgal, which would fit the north; the Hebrew text is followed here.

records.source: מֶ֥לֶךְ תִּרְצָ֖ה אֶחָ֑ד כָּל־מְלָכִ֖ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְאֶחָֽד׃פ
records.gloss: King of Tirzah, one; all [the] kings, thirty and one.
pieces: the king of Tirzah, one. Thirty-one kings in all.

L.24: the king of Tirzah, one. All the kings: thirty-one.

R.24: the king of Tirzah, one. There were thirty-one kings in all.

decisions.choice: Tirzah: a town of the central hills
decisions.reason: Tirzah is not named in the battle accounts. It later became a royal city of the northern kingdom (1 Kings 14:17; 15:33).

decisions.choice: thirty-one kings in all: a count of kings defeated, not of towns fully held
decisions.reason: The total sums the tally of "one" in verses 9-24. Defeating a town's king did not always mean Israel held the town: Jerusalem and Gezer stayed in Canaanite hands (15:63; 16:10), and much land was still left to take (13:1).

decisions.choice: Thirty-one kings in all
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "all kings, thirty-one". Balanced and Readable put the number first, as a total is usually given.
